note: Machine-readable mirror of the owner's preferences. If this file and CLAUDE.md disagree, CLAUDE.md wins. check: auto = measurable by a script; visual = needs a frame review; plan = decided before building; process = how the studio works.

upload.video: H.264 high, CRF 17, maxrate 26M, yuv420p bt709 tv-range, fast-start

audio.loop: built circularly; room tone/drone across the wrap; mastered on a wrapped copy; audio length == video length (<= 1 frame)
audio.music: edited on the half-beat grid; tape-stop or dead stop allowed as an ending; splices on the beat grid with 12 ms equal-power crossfade
audio.dialogue: Demucs vocal stem, cleaned, levelled, equal-power fades at every join
audio.sfx: every transition has its own layered sound (whoosh + impact + a material); no loud sound on every cut

picture.sharpness_check: tools/sharpness.py packs (while picking) and N (finished video): swap shots below 0.80x the edit median

text.ease_in: fade + rise + blur-to-sharp, ~0.17 s; nothing pops on
text.standard_style: v9 NIGHT BLOOM construction (Inter Display Black caps, two lines ~88/114 px, dark keyline ~7 % of size, soft shadow, light scrim, emphasis colour with glow, word-timed)
text.hero_title: per-letter build on a shared baseline, its own designed animation acting out the meaning
text.timing: every lyric word on its sung onset, verified on the Demucs vocal stem (pitch + onsets), not Whisper alone
text.explicit_lyrics: use two designed titles, not captions
never: thin wide-tracked editorial sans with serif-italic emphasis (v8)

branding.as: a transition (slam in, fly through the 'o'): tin=logo_orig

loop.method: the last frames are built from frame 0's own image; the loop is a set piece from the character's world

structure.song_section: the good part (song_map.py): the drop where the full mix or bass returns at ~33-47 % of the edit
structure.opening: strong in the first 1-2 s; dialogue openings play as one continuous take (J-cuts, dissolves, matched-angle morph)

transitions.plain_cuts: none in quiet or dialogue sections
transitions.feel: going through something; viewer asks 'how did they do that'
transitions.repeat: never, except as a deliberate motif

dialogue.rule: one or two short lines that set up the song; let the visuals carry the ending

only_when: lit like real objects or from real footage
props.check: stills next to the footage; rebuild or cut anything that looks drawn

motion.velocity: tmap=vel(...), lin=True, interp='flow' on every hook/montage shot (burst on the beat, flow slow motion between)

beat_camera.hit_frames: zoom blur + colour split, type kept clean

motion.beat_moments: no shot only 'moves to the beat': give each a beat animation (aura, remnants, charge-up) with its own sound

concept.rule: one concept tying picture, sound, text and the loop; found in the material (the song's own words, the character's history); Dexter edits rooted in Dexter's world (kill room, plastic, slides, tools, the Code, the Dark Passenger, victims)
concept.assets: hero graphics detailed, lit to the shot, revealed physically on real tracked objects; checked at full resolution

loop: one video qc per revision (later revisions re-render only what changed)
visual sign-off on the encoded file
vrender.py N clean at the verdict
review_gates: automated QC on the encoded MP4 (qcN.py)
contact sheets around every transition and title
final pull of key frames from the encoded file
sharpness check on the finished video
workflow.pre_build_gate: compare the plan shot by shot with the benchmarks; redesign until it clearly beats them
workflow.efficiency: one brief, one feedback message per revision, one full render per revision

communication.progress: short lines, no long code in chat
final_message: ask the owner to watch once with sound
communication.honesty: cannot watch or listen: report what was verified by frames and measurement

benchmarks.reference_for: concept from the material, one focal set piece, detailed physical hero assets, beat moments, exact loop landing
benchmarks.quote: I like this edit and would like for you to make it a standard.

benchmarks.reference_for: concept from the lyric × the character's double life; light behind the subject; the loop as the most creative transition; Dexter scaffold base
benchmarks.quote: I like this edit and would like for you to make it a standard. The only gripe I have is the quality of some of the clips.
I like this edit and would like for you to make it a standard.
The transitions were creative and well animated.

benchmarks.reference_for: amount and quality of transitions, animations, graphics; music-led structure; text
benchmarks.quote: wonderful transitions, animations, graphics, while maintaining the style that I like… I like how the music correlates to the edit. I like the text.

benchmarks.reference_for: dialogue-led opening as one continuous take; barrel to scope; pupil to iris loop

rejected.what: name labels; stamp under captions; text popping on; watermark; outro card
rejected.rule: no labels; ease every word; logo once; no outro

rejected.what: BLEED IT unreadable; sloppy cut before a line
rejected.rule: check text on stills; designed joins in dialogue

rejected.what: starburst/explosion transition; title card; slow-mo run-at-camera and floating shots; wrong lyric; weak falling letters
rejected.rule: themed bursts only; no title cards; cut odd footage; verify lyrics on the stem; multi-stage text

rejected.what: rapid single-word dialogue run; talking jar-of-blood shot; 'I'm a serial killer' ending; strings converging on his face with a target ring; blue (recoloured) logo; plain steel doors for CLOSE
rejected.rule: 1-2 lines; every shot earns its place; visuals carry the ending; no face gimmicks; never restyle the logo; themed detailed text moments

rejected.what: thin wide-tracked sans + serif-italic emphasis, letter-by-letter fades, underlines, extruded words behind his head
lacklustre: concept from the song title (petals, moon), soft not dark; generic quick moves; one set piece; thin graphics
rejected.rule: concept from the character's world; 3+ set pieces; graphics in every section

rejected.what: lacklustre twice; lit-up-eyes shot; frozen-scene glass shatter; whirlwind CARRY OFF exit; plain rewind loop
rejected.rule: motion pass; props rule; loop as a set piece

rejected.what: blood slides lingering as an overlay; random drips/spatter/knife on beats; drawn-looking slides; glass web over his face; flat duct tape
rejected.rule: props only when motivated, brief, real-looking, in the look, off the face

rejected.what: soft shots (sunrise walk zoomed ~3.5x, palms, lollipop, ice cream, hood, pink wall)
rejected.rule: sharpness check; zoom <= 10 % on 720p; close-ups on the least-compressed packs

rejected.what: the sun drawn over the whole frame burned away the top of his head; soft clips at the verdict
rejected.rule: light behind the subject; clip-quality ranking

qc_gates.check: every face centred, none cut by the frame edge
no face box inside an active text band (flags checked on frames)
no audio clicks at any cut or the loop seam
loop seam picture blurred diff <= 1.0; audio continuous
audio and video same length (<= 1 frame)
before rendering: sharpness.py N --src (SOFT < 0.80x median, zoom > 10 %, LOWBIT < 800 kb/s); after: sharpness.py N
no white-out runs (mean luma >= 200 for 2+ frames); <= 3 flashes a second; flashes peaking over 110 listed for a visual check
no source range leaks past a source cut
frames from the encoded file around every transition, title, the drop and the loop look right
after any engine change: golden frames of v10 and v11 within max 2/255 per pixel, mean < 0.2/255
a partial re-render is used only if ~30 frames outside its range re-render bit-exact against the frame cache; otherwise full render
list runs where > 3 % of the face box gains > 0.10 luma (outside transitions); review each on the sheet; fix any that isn't a designed moment
no transition or set piece with effects more than 12 dB under the music (loudest 50 ms of effects vs music RMS)

engine_bases.note: agreed between the studios 2026-11-07; shared effects ported through handoffs

rules_from_handoffs.rule: Light sources go behind the subject: the person matte, light only from the background, a light wrap on the near edge.
rules_from_handoffs.evidence: what happened with the sun and the top right part of dexters head? (v105 rev 1)

rules_from_handoffs.rule: Clip quality: restore 720p; rank sources before choosing (sharpness.py N --src) and on the render; zoom <= 1.1; hero shots on high-bitrate packs; ask for 1080p/4K packs for hero moments.
rules_from_handoffs.evidence: The only gripe I have is the quality of some of the clips (v105 verdict)

rules_from_handoffs.rule: The loop is the most creative transition in the edit: a set piece paying off the concept, landing in frame 0's own image.
rules_from_handoffs.evidence: make it a more creative and unique transition (v105 rev 2-3)

rules_from_handoffs.rule: Restyle library transitions before reusing them.
rules_from_handoffs.evidence: v105 rev 3 review (v6 cube grid, v9 jasmine)

rules_from_handoffs.rule: When a burn/dissolve removes the subject, remove him before drawing scene light; fill the hole with plausible background.
'Add transitions, graphics and animations wherever possible' = replace generic connectors with themed ones and add new cuts with new transitions.
Mix effects against how loudly the song is mastered: measure at every set piece; on a loud master push effects ~+9 dB and duck the music ~3 dB under the biggest hits.
rules_from_handoffs.evidence: v105 effects first sat 20-25 dB under the song (rev 1 review)
